siatka.label: Siatka
siatka.note: The workbench: the application views grid with every panel, as before P20. Dawny „Warsztat” (kod: layout workshop). W3: drawn from this dock tree (list | chat over knowledge, 0.32 as the former 32 % chat strip); the former header is the switcher bar; the panels are its tabs and open as windows over the layout.
siatka.leaf_sizing_note: W3: a leaf whose window keeps its own size (the conversation list: its CSS width and collapse, as in the former Workshop); other leaves take the split ratio. A preset: 'ratio' gives the list 22 %.

fallbacks_note: W5: layout_mode=windows means 'the last own layout' (OKNA §3.1): the layout active on this device class (window_layout_active) when it is an own one, else the most recently saved (window_layouts); only when the person has saved none does it open this fallback, the grid. A preset, not a rule.
panel_kinds_note: W1: which window kind a panel of the app opens as (maximized over the layout, OKNA §3.3). Open map: a panel missing here opens as the kind of its own id.
window_words_note: W2: a word of a sentence (folded, no diacritics) to a window: the longest stem a word starts with wins; the value is `chat` (the own chat window) or a panel id. Open map, an example set; an id of a panel is accepted as is.
window_placements_note: W2: the placement a screen uses for an asked one, per device class (`any` = every class). Preset: every placement is the next maximized window of the stack (OKNA §4.1) until docking and floating are drawn (W3/W4); the receipt says so when it differs from the asked one. A preset, not a rule. W5: the settings field of the same name (settings_fields.pack) overrides this preset when it is set.
window_back_note: W2 (OKNA §4.2): what Back does with windows: visits (back to the previous window of the journal of visits), to_chat (back to the chat window), close_window (closes the window in front), none (Back never changes the window). Preset of the phone. W5: the settings field of the same name (settings_fields.pack) overrides this preset when it is set.
window_restore_last_note: W2: the start view `last_saved` restores the windows of the last session (window_layout_last in localStorage loom.shell.last.v2), not only the layout id. false = only the layout id, as in W1. W5: the settings field of the same name (settings_fields.pack) overrides this preset when it is set.
window_restore_front_note: W2: which window is in front after a start that restored window_layout_last: layout (preset: the window the layout's preset maximizes, the chat; the restored others wait in the switcher - a start looks as before W2) | saved (the window that was in front when the page was left). W5: the settings field of the same name (settings_fields.pack) overrides this preset when it is set.

text.pl: Zadokowane okna mają tu mniej niż {min} px szerokości ({widths}).
text.en: Docked windows are narrower than {min} px here ({widths}).

text.pl: Okno «{title}» jest w większości poza ekranem.
text.en: The window «{title}» is mostly off the screen.

window_arrange_note: W4 (OKNA §4.4, §6.3): presets of docking and floating - thresholds of the advisories dock_narrow (min_useful_width px of a drawn leaf), float_offscreen (fraction of a floating rect outside the area), float_under_keyboard (on-screen keyboard at least keyboard_min_px tall); drop_edge = the fraction of a leaf near its edge that docks to that side (the middle makes a tab); the menu entries and keys reach every arrangement without dragging. All examples; any value works, also degenerate ones (0 = never narrow).
device_classes_note: W5: the device class of a screen (the key of window_layout_active and of window_layout_journal): the first rule whose width range (CSS px, max_width / min_width) holds the screen wins. An open list of examples - add tablet, tv, watch… as rules; a screen no rule holds is the class `any`.
layout_reset_note: W5: what „Jak w aplikacji” (layout.reset) brings back, per device class (`any` = every class): `same` = the shipped form of the layout drawn now (czat stays czat, siatka stays siatka), or the id of a shipped layout. One journal entry, undo returns the layout that was there.
journal_limit_note: W5: the bound of the persisted journal (window_layout_journal, per device class); the field's own `limit` overrides it. Any number ≥ 0 (0 = no undo).
journal_writers_note: W5b: how many writers (tabs, each with its own client id) keep their own journal in window_layout_journal.writers; past it the record updated longest ago is dropped when a writer saves (its entries are a copy of layout states, the layouts themselves stay). The value's own `writers_limit` overrides it; 0 = no bound.
journal_inherit_note: W5b: where a writer with no journal of its own (a new tab) takes its starting copy from, in order: `installation` = the most recently updated writer of the same browser installation and device class, `person` = the most recently updated writer of that class anywhere, then the W5 per-class journal. An open list; [] = a new tab starts with an empty journal. The value's own `inherit` overrides it.
active_levels_note: W5b (OKNA D19): where the page writes the active own layout of a device class (window_layout_active): `installation` = installations.<installation id>.<class> (this browser only; an empty id = no own layout here, which wins over the person value), `person` = <class> (the fallback of every installation that has no value of its own). Reading always tries this installation first, then the person value. An open list; the value's own `levels` overrides it.
window_sides_note: W7: the words of a sentence for a side (window.dock) or a direction (window.move), folded (no diacritics, lower case), to left/right/top/bottom. An open list of examples: a language or a synonym is one more entry; a word not listed is answered (the receipt names it), nothing is guessed.
window_step_note: W7: presets of the sentences window.move (step in px when the sentence names no number) and window.resize (factor per word; a number scales both sides, {w,h} each side). Any value, also degenerate ones (0 = the window collapses to nothing, which the float_offscreen advisory then says).

window_mount.keep_mounted_note: W10 (OKNA §8.3): presets of the settings field window_keep_mounted per device class (an open value: visible | all | recent:<n>; unset = this preset). visible everywhere = what the host did before W10 (hidden windows unmounted, state from state_keys); the design named `all` as a desktop preset - kept `visible` until a measurement shows `all` buys something (the W10 harness measures both, card S1 / M1-OKNA-W10). Reversal: one value here.
window_mount.mounted_soft_note: W10: the advisory many_windows asks when more windows are mounted than this number on a device class (any number ≥ 0; a class without a number is never asked). A preset, not a cap: nothing is refused or unmounted by itself.
window_mount.cost_estimate_note: W10: the estimate shown as evidence of many_windows - JS heap per mounted window measured by e2e/windows-perf-native.mjs (a dated observation of one machine and browser, never a constraint; WebView on a phone is not measured here).
window_mount.restore_frames_note: W10: for how many animation frames (≈ 5 s at 60 Hz) a remounted window tries to restore its kept scroll while its content loads (a panel that fetches its data first shows „Wczytuję…”); it stops at once when every position is restored or the person touches the window. Any number ≥ 0.

text.pl: Zamontowanych okien: {count} (podpowiedź od {soft}); szacunek pamięci ok. {mb} MB (pomiar {observed}).
text.en: Mounted windows: {count} (advice from {soft}); estimated memory about {mb} MB (measured {observed}).

text.pl: Wartość «{value}» pola window_keep_mounted nie jest znana; użyto «{used}».
text.en: The value «{value}» of window_keep_mounted is not known; «{used}» is used.
